metadata.title: SimCSE: Simple Contrastive Learning of Sentence Embeddings

problem.value: Pre-trained word embeddings suffer from anisotropy issues.

evidence.quote: We also draw a connection to the recent findings that pre-trained word embeddings suffer from anisotropy (Ethayarajh, 2019;Li et al., 2020) and prove that-through a spectrum perspective-the contrastive learning objective "flattens" the singular value distribution of the sentence embedding space, hence improving uniformity.

contributions.value: We present SimCSE, a simple contrastive learning framework that advances state-of-the-art sentence embeddings.

evidence.quote: This paper presents SimCSE, a simple contrastive learning framework that greatly advances state-of-the-art sentence embeddings.

contributions.value: We describe an unsupervised approach using standard dropout as noise.

evidence.quote: We first describe an unsupervised approach, which takes an input sentence and predicts itself in a contrastive objective, with only standard dropout used as noise.

contributions.value: We propose a supervised approach incorporating natural language inference datasets into contrastive learning.

evidence.quote: Then, we propose a supervised approach, which incorporates annotated pairs from natural language inference datasets into our contrastive learning framework by using "entailment" pairs as positives and "contradiction" pairs as hard negatives.

task.value: Learning universal sentence embeddings and evaluating on semantic textual similarity tasks.

evidence.quote: Learning universal sentence embeddings is a fundamental problem in natural language processing and has been studied extensively in the literature (Kiros et al., 2015;Hill et al., 2016;Conneau et al., 2017;Logeswaran and Lee, 2018;Cer et al., 2018;Reimers and Gurevych, 2019, inter alia).

method_summary.value: Sentences are encoded using a pre-trained language model such as BERT or RoBERTa.

evidence.quote: In this work, we encode input sentences using a pre-trained language model such as BERT (Devlin et al., 2019) or RoBERTa (Liu et al., 2019): h = f θ (x), and then fine-tune all the parameters using the contrastive learning objective (Eq. 1).

method_summary.value: Unsupervised SimCSE uses identical sentences as positive pairs, relying on independently sampled standard dropout masks in Transformers as noise.

evidence.quote: The idea of unsupervised SimCSE is extremely simple: we take a collection of sentences {x i } m i=1 and use x + i = x i .

method_summary.value: Supervised SimCSE leverages entailment pairs from NLI datasets as positive examples and incorporates contradiction pairs as hard negatives.

evidence.quote: Formally, we extend (x i , x + i ) to (x i , x + i , x - i ) , where x i is the premise, x + i and x - i are entailment and contradiction hypotheses.

novelty.value: Using standard dropout on intermediate representations outperforms discrete data augmentation operators in NLP contrastive learning.

evidence.quote: As we will see in §3, simply using standard dropout on intermediate representations outperforms these discrete operators.

datasets.value: 7 semantic textual similarity tasks including STS 2012-2016, STS Benchmark, and SICK-Relatedness

evidence.quote: We evaluate on 7 STS tasks: STS 2012-2016 (Agirre et al., 2012(Agirre et al., , 2013(Agirre et al., , 2014(Agirre et al., , 2015(Agirre et al., , 2016)), STS Benchmark (Cer et al., 2017) and SICK-Relatedness (Marelli et al., 2014).

evidence.quote: We train unsupervised SimCSE on 10 6 randomly sampled sentences from English Wikipedia, and train supervised SimCSE on the combination of MNLI and SNLI datasets (314k).

claims.value: Unsupervised and supervised BERT base models achieve high average Spearman's correlation on STS tasks representing improvements over previous best results.

evidence.quote: We evaluate SimCSE on standard semantic textual similarity (STS) tasks, and our unsupervised and supervised models using BERT base achieve an average of 76.3% and 81.6% Spearman's correlation respectively, a 4.2% and 2.2% improvement compared to the previous best results.
